aApi.title: Model APIs (overview)
aApi.body:
An API lets your program ask the model for you: send text, get a reply.

📍 Location: Model APIs › Model APIs (overview)
⚙️ Usage layer: no model parameters change, only how you use it
🧪 Try it:

🎯 Role

  • The program attaches a key and sends the request to the platform’s address.
  • The platform’s model replies, along with the usage (token counts).

▶ How to use it

  • Sign up → create a key → find the address, model name and price → first request → set a spending limit.

🧠 Why it’s designed this way (the logic underneath)

To put a model into your own site, script or tool, you use an API.

✅ Why this works

No GPU to buy; pay for what you use.

⚠️ Limits / notes: Your data goes to the platform; it needs the network; heavy use costs per token.

aKey.title: API key
aKey.body:
A string that proves “it is you; bill me”: effectively your wallet.

📍 Location: Model APIs › API key
⚙️ Usage layer: no model parameters change, only how you use it
🧪 Try it:

🎯 Role

  • Put it in the request header and the platform answers and bills you.

▶ How to use it

  • Keep it only in an environment variable or the server’s secret store; read it at run time.
  • Never in code, never in front-end code, never pasted into a chat.

🧠 Why it’s designed this way (the logic underneath)

Whoever holds the key spends your money.

✅ Why this works

With a spending limit and one key per project, a leak stays contained.

⚠️ Limits / notes: After a leak you can only delete and recreate it; money already spent is usually gone.

aCompat.title: OpenAI-compatible format
aCompat.body:
Many platforms (and local runners) accept the same request format; the same code moves by changing three things.

📍 Location: Model APIs › OpenAI-compatible format
⚙️ Usage layer: no model parameters change, only how you use it
🧪 Try it:

🎯 Role

  • Change base_url (address), api_key (key) and model (name).
  • messages is a list of “who said what”: system, user, assistant.

▶ How to use it

  • Check that the platform documents compatibility; otherwise follow its own docs.

🧠 Why it’s designed this way (the logic underneath)

One format makes switching platforms or going local easy.

✅ Why this works

Local runners such as Ollama and vLLM offer it too.

⚠️ Limits / notes: “Compatible” usually covers the common features; details differ.

aPrice.title: Paying by tokens
aPrice.body:
Bill = input tokens × input price + output tokens × output price, priced per million tokens.

📍 Location: Model APIs › Paying by tokens
⚙️ Usage layer: no model parameters change, only how you use it
🧪 Try it:

🎯 Role

  • Output usually costs several times more than input.
  • Input whose start matches an earlier request may be billed at a cheaper “cache hit” price.

▶ How to use it

  • Read usage in the reply: prompt_tokens and completion_tokens.

🧠 Why it’s designed this way (the logic underneath)

The model reads and writes tokens, and spends compute per token.

✅ Why this works

Dropping irrelevant material, asking for short answers and putting fixed content first all save money.

⚠️ Limits / notes: The same text has different token counts on different models; estimates are estimates.
